title: CH Robinson to Buy RXO for $5.8 Billion in Bet on AI Model
source_used: Supply Chain Dive (its own report from the companies' news release and investor presentation) and DC Velocity. Bloomberg page (the pool item) blocked (HTTP 403).
key_facts: C.H. Robinson Worldwide plans to acquire brokerage and transportation services provider RXO in a stock-and-cash transaction valued at $5.8 billion, announced in a news release on Monday 5 Oct 2026.

The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and approval by RXO shareholders; the companies say the combination would create an over-$25-billion third-party logistics company.
C.H. Robinson CEO Dave Bozeman says the combined network would bring together about 93,000 shippers and 600,000 carriers.

C.H. Robinson would apply its 'Lean AI' operating model and deploy AI agents across RXO's workflows, for an expected $300 million of net run-rate savings within two years of closing; other savings would come from real-estate consolidation and moving RXO's external services to existing C.H. Robinson vendors.
RXO has limited shipper overlap with C.H. Robinson; its revenue comes mainly from retail and e-commerce, industrial and manufacturing, and food and beverage customers.
Orbis Investments, RXO's largest shareholder, supports the deal; RXO was split off from XPO in 2021 and bought UPS's freight brokerage Coyote Logistics for $1.025 billion in 2024 (DC Velocity).
2026 estimates: C.H. Robinson gross revenue $18.4 billion and RXO $6.8 billion (Supply Chain Dive table).
quote_evidence: C.H. Robinson Worldwide plans to acquire brokerage and transportation services provider RXO in a stock-and-cash transaction valued at $5.8 billion, the companies announced in a news release Monday.
The deal, which is expected to close in the first half of 2027, is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory clearance and approval by RXO shareholders.

If the acquisition is approved, C.H. Robinson will implement its "Lean AI" operating model and deploy artificial intelligence agents across RXO's workflows, helping create an expected $300 million of net run-rate savings within two years of the deal closing.
why_it_matters_hint: Two large US freight brokers would combine, and the buyer plans to use AI agents to cut about $300 million a year in costs.
notes: Bloomberg's page (the pool item) could not be opened, so Supply Chain Dive, which reported from the companies' news release and investor presentation, is credited; DC Velocity read as a cross-check. Savings and network figures are the companies' own.
